doc.title: Al Tinney interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002

title: School arrangements and Porgy & Bess pay
summary: Special school privileges, and ten dollars a week per child, twenty with his brother, under a manager's contract.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Well it must have been a little hard for you to function well in school, wasn’t it? When you were doing these shows and things? © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

No because they made special privileges. They took me out of one school and put me in another school that was mainly for kids who were working — something — I don’t know how it was turned around, but anyhow I know I had certain days out of school. I think I went maybe to school one day a week or so, something like that. Well because there was a performance every day.
Do you recall what you got paid?
Ten dollars I think it was.
This is what this manager, who had all of us kids under contract, this is all the kids got. That’s all.
Was it ten dollars per show or ten dollars per week?

No ten dollars per week. This guy was — he was reaping up the money man. But he had a separate contract with the management of the theater and a separate one with us, showing the mothers and things how much — see I mean in those days that was a bit of money, in those days. You could do something. And my brother and I were in it so it was double.
And the way your mother was, she could really stretch that.
Yeah man, she was great with it. She was great with it. Yeah. So it wasn’t hard. We were doing what she wanted us to do. She wanted us to be in show business and we just went ahead and did it.
She must have been happy, at least at that point.
